metadata.title: Where Apple is diverging from rest of Mag 7 earnings

content.text:
Apple (AAPL) stock continues to drop on Friday while shares of Amazon (AMZN) surge since the two tech giants posted earnings results yesterday.
Morning Brief Host Julie Hyman is joined by Yahoo Finance Breaking News Reporter Jake Conley and Trustless Media Founder Zack Guzman take a closer look at the key figures that Apple reported in its earnings release.
So let's talk about Apple and Amazon here. Um, and you know, Apple, it seems to me the bottom line here is that the memory chip shortage is hurting Apple. That's what's starting to happen. Even with Apple's enormous size, enormous leverage, um in terms of its negotiating power that they're basically saying like we cannot make enough. And it's not just memory chips, it's their other types, it's their full chip set
that they can't get enough of it to keep up with demand.
Yeah, I think this week was very interesting just to kind of compare the moves and you can look at earlier in the week when you saw Microsoft and and meta kind of break. similar story with Amazon and Apple and kind of really starting to figure out how much do we know about the the payoffs. Like are these investments actually going anywhere? You saw the reaction to meta last uh well it was earlier this week. If you don't have any goods to show for it, it's a very tough day. And and I would agree with with with Amazon, we can get into that one later, but like that was a very positive uh earnings report. For Apple, I think short-term yes, a lot of questions around how much of a supply constraint and like Apple usually has so much power over everyone but in this cycle not so much.
Well, you can't make things, you know, you can't make them make things that they can't make.
Yes. That's right. That sounds very smart. Supply constraints are very real. But
But but also to your point, I thought this was reading the two calls, I thought it was really interesting between Apple and Amazon.
Because Apple, as is its want, is not very specific. Analysts ask them questions and they kind of say, yes, Siri AI is going to be great. But okay, and, whereas Amazon gets really specific about the products that it's offering, about the runway of its spend and what it's going to look like. And, you know, similarly, Meta was like, we're going to develop agents, but we don't have them yet. Whereas Amazon's like, here is our agent. It's called, what is it called? Q, I think. Um, here is what it does. Here are the list of clients that we already have for it.
Here's our order backlog that's tripling year over year.
Right, exactly. So much more specific.
Well, Apple has a little bit there in terms of things to look forward to, but I think, yes, the point of, you know, it being Tim Cook's final earnings call leaves a lot of, okay, what comes next? And kind of almost like a little bit of the hesitation around a new Fed chair coming in is the market needs to figure out how are we actually going to learn what's really going on at Apple. But I mean, if you look ahead, still optimistic to be uh to be trading around iPhone price increases that are probably going to be coming in September as well with the new iPhone too. So I I don't know. I I think, you know, just to echo the buying the dips here anytime you see weakness from these tech companies, I feel like it's a good time.
It's worked out well for most most of them.
So far, that's right. It's kept working, but to your point, Zach, at some point, and this is what we keep saying on the show every single day, you've got to show the ROI. You've got to be able to go to your investors and say, look, here's what we're actually getting out of this. Amazon bumped its uh CAPEX projections for the year up to approximately $220 billion. That's adding about 20 billion from previous projections, and the stock is rewarded for it. And not just for that, they had really good numbers,
but it's okay to keep spending more if you can show you're getting the return.
Well, I would say another couple of things on this. Um and our our um our senior producer asked this this morning, like, what's different between Amazon and Alphabet? Like Alphabet said negative free cash flow too, and that stock was punished. Even though its cloud business was up 82%. So, Amazon's negative free cash flow, $7.6 billion. I think there are two real differences. One, if you are a long time investor in Amazon, you're used to this to some extent. The numbers are bigger on the spending side, but Amazon periodically has negative free cash flow. It's not that unusual. It tends to like ramp up spending and then pull it back. Um so that's thing one. Thing two is, Amazon has the luxury of coming after Alphabet and after Meta. And so, you know, A, we've already seen a sell off. And B, the market is sort of more habituated now after hearing those earlier reports. So, I I think those are the two things that are making it maybe a little easier.
That's a really good point. I think also when you're accustomed to kind of like how these companies are situated, I think, you know, listening to Zuck on their earnings call too earlier this week, it's to your point, it's like, look, we don't know where the value is going to come from eventually, but like if you think about what Meta is downstream, like their whole model is built around scale and actually reaching users, which, you know, it's a very different stage than right now and we're talking about actually investing in the data centers and everything else. And so I think, you know, if I were looking at all the results, to your point Julie, like Microsoft having, what I think it was the most value we've seen added by a company in a single day, 450 billion, not bad. And I think that that's kind of the stage we're in is like, if you can show the results right now, you'll be rewarded and if it's a little bit farther out, like a meta and you have to wait, you know, good luck in the interim.
And it's also a question whether the growth is accelerating or decelerating or uncertain, right? And so I think like you can also use that metric for these various companies to try and assess how they're going to um how they're going to do.
So, okay, so now between Ash and Brenner and and we've gotten most of the hyperscalers or all of the hyperscalers. We still, I guess we still have to wait for Oracle, right? And we have to wait for Oracle's a different cadence. NVIDIA will come eventually. But like is everything okay now?
Well, I was thinking back to like, remember when we chatted about the IBM warning a few weeks ago and it was like, hey, uh everyone's spending on all the chips and stuff. No one really cares about software. That's a good kind of like blend of all these stories because it was kind of built into the idea of betting hard on chips and kind of shorting software. And then that works until you have massive volatility and it all blows up. And so I think that the trend is still very much intact around kind of what that warning signal and we saw it from Apple too, is there's a lot of demand for these chips and building kind of your investment decisions around that thesis, I think is smart and that is not changing anytime soon.
Even if Ashton Brenner's fund
is gone there. Even if it blows up. But it still buying that.
You saw me on the other day, because he's buying the dip, because he's got the capital to deploy and he's also got the room in the fund to say, look, these assets are cheap. We know even if there's a temporary pullback, the momentum is almost certainly not going anywhere. The demand, we're not seeing it slow down. So let's buy now when we can get it cheap.
I mean, I mean, that seems to be the bet that everybody is now, not everybody, but the market is now making that bet judging by what's happening in the futures this morning.
